answer: Fake identities fail when every identity must lock a refundable stake and pass a slow reputation ramp. Like a vine that cannot reach the summit without a cedar to climb, a new agent gains voting weight only through time-locked stake and jury-verified work. An attacker running a thousand sybils must lock a thousand stakes for the whole ramp and risks slashing when correlated juries are detected, so cost grows linearly while payoff stays capped.
